references.text: Moses' song mentions that Israel sacrificed to demons (שֵׁדִים) who were not God, showing the same idolatry as sacrificing to שְּׂעִירִם (goat-demons) in Leviticus.
Jeroboam appointed priests for שְּׂעִירִם (goat-demons) and the calves he had made, a direct reference to the prohibition against sacrificing to these demons.
The psalm describes how Israel sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons, showing the idolatry the verse warns against.
Isaiah prophesies that שְׂעִירִים (goat-demons) will dance in ruined Babylon, showing the demonic nature of these beings.
Isaiah mentions that a שָׂעִיר will call to its companion in ruined Edom, a reference to the same demonic beings.
Ezekiel describes Israel's spiritual adultery (זָנָה) with idols, the same term used in the verse about being unfaithful to God.
Ezekiel uses the metaphor of prostitution (זְנוּנִים) to describe Israel's idolatry, paralleling the language in Leviticus about committing whoredom after goat-demons.
Revelation mentions that people did not repent from worshipping demons, showing the persistent sin that Leviticus warned against.
